### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A33 was followed by A16 (about 49 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) or A17 (about 52 in 100); in the later window it is followed by A14 (about 53 in 100) or A15 (about 48 in 100) instead. [DIR006]
- In the earlier window, A14 and A15 each ran in about half of the traces (roughly 103 and 97 of 200), about two-thirds of the way through each trace (mean position about 0.67), and all of their observed outgoing transitions led to A23. In the later window they run about one-third of the way through (mean about 0.36) and all of their observed outgoing transitions lead to A18. [DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002]
- In the earlier window, A16 and A17 ran in every trace at about position 0.38, in a mixed mutual order, leading either to each other or to A18 (A16 to A18 in about 52 in 100 of its transitions, A17 to A18 in about 49 in 100). In the later window they run at about position 0.65, still in a mixed mutual order, and lead either to each other or to A23 (A16 to A23 about 48 in 100, A17 to A23 about 53 in 100). [DIR003, DIR004, POS003, POS004]
- In the earlier window, A22 (mean position about 0.64) was followed by A14 (about 52 in 100) or A15 (about 49 in 100), and A23 followed exactly two steps after A22 in all 200 traces. In the later window, A22 (mean position about 0.60) is followed by A16 (about 53 in 100) or A17 (about 48 in 100), and A23 follows exactly three steps after A22 in all 200 traces. [DIR005, LAG001, POS006]
- The distance from A33 to A18 shrank from three steps to two. [LAG002]
- The relative order flipped for every pair spanning the two segments: A16 and A17 preceded A18 and A22 in 100 of 100 traces earlier, whereas A18 and A22 precede A16 and A17 in 100 of 100 traces later; likewise, A16/A17/A18/A22 preceded A14 in the roughly 52 in 100 traces where both occurred (about 49 in 100 for A15) earlier, whereas in the later window A14 and A15 come first where they co-occur (about 53 and 48 in 100). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- A18 and A22 each shifted slightly earlier (mean position from about 0.43 to 0.40 and from about 0.64 to 0.60). [POS005, POS006]
- Participation and branch sizes stayed essentially the same: A16, A17, A18, A22 and A33 occur in every trace in both windows, A14 and A15 each in about half, and the A14-versus-A15 and A16-versus-A17 splits remain within about four points in 100 of their earlier values. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two existing segments exchanged their places in the execution sequence. Earlier, the either-or choice between A14 and A15 sat between A22 and A23 (each alternative followed by A23), while the pair A16 and A17, executed in a mixed order, sat between A33 and A18; in the later window, the A14/A15 choice sits directly after A33 and leads to A18, while the A16/A17 pair sits between A22 and A23 and leads to A23 — A33 and A22 effectively exchanged their successors, and A18 and A23 received new predecessors. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]

This is shown directly, not inferred from frequencies alone: deterministic order reversals in 100 of 100 traces for all four pairs spanning the boundary (A16/A17 against A18/A22), reversed precedence between A14/A15 and the A16/A17/A18/A22 group, exact lag changes (A33 to A18 from three steps to two; A22 to A23 from two to three), and matching position shifts (A14/A15 earlier, A16/A17 later, A18/A22 slightly earlier). All 22 qualified items fit this single reordering, far more than the roughly 0.36 items expected by chance among the 72 tested units, and each segment keeps its internal behaviour (mixed A16/A17 order, an about half-half A14/A15 choice, unchanged participation), which argues against a mere shift in how often existing paths are taken. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, LAG001, LAG002, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]

Limitations: positions and lags are event ranks within traces, not clock times, so the hypothesis concerns execution order rather than timing; and only the eight flagged activities are covered, so the evidence cannot rule out that further activities located between A18 and A22, or elsewhere around the swapped segments, also moved — the exact block boundaries outside the observed activities remain unverified. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, LAG001, LAG002]

Other differences: none beyond the above; no activity appeared or disappeared and no branch share moved by more than about four points in 100, so the change resembles a relocation of two existing segments rather than added, removed or re-frequenced paths. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
